correctness.rationale: Exact definitions and quantifiers cover every pair of labeled STS(9). The disjoint matching argument identifies all legal six-cycle flips with the 36 label-transposition moves. The stabilizer is explicitly enumerated as AGL(2,3) of order 432; finite exact-cover enumeration of the 840 systems proves every system is an affine relabeling. Minimum transposition word length equals nine minus cycle count, so exhaustive evaluation of all 840 cosets against all 432 stabilizer elements gives exact upper and lower switch distances. An independently constructed exact-cover graph computes all 840 BFS layers and all 705,600 ordered pair distances, checking the same intersection map. Scripts and logged stdout are included and reproduced. Theorem is finite; no extrapolation is used.

originality.rationale: The 1999 paper of Grannell, Griggs and Murphy explicitly establishes connectedness and the total 840 labeled STS(9) configurations; those are prior results. Lindner–Rosa's intersection spectrum, reproduced by Chee–Ling–Shen, is also prior. The accepted claim newly identifies the geodesic distance for every pair as an exact function of shared blocks, including diameter three and the complete metric census. Direct comparison of pertinent accessible primary full text and overlapping modern results found no equivalent distance theorem. Publication priority beyond checked sources remains uncertain.
residual_risks: The full content of some supplementary relevant publications was unavailable or only partially read.
A geodesic classification under different wording or an unpublished computation may exist; absence from searches is not proof of novelty.

value.rationale: Six-cycle switching is a pre-existing, natural reconfiguration operation on Steiner triple systems. Earlier order-nine connectivity and intersection spectrum do not determine minimum switch counts. The new complete exact metric classification assigns an optimal transition cost to each of 705,600 ordered pairs using the natural common-block invariant. It identifies disjoint pairs as sharp distance-three witnesses and can guide exact schedule/design transformations. This is a meaningful complete finite classification, not an arbitrary isolated parameter or repetition of a known connectivity proof.
